text_fidelity_a:
TP-Link AC1900 Smart Wireless Router - Beamforming Dual Band Gigabit WiFi Internet Routers for Home, High Speed, Long Range, Ideal for Gaming (Archer C9) Got this to manage the wireless network of a family member. I'm disappointed by limitations which I describe below. After all of it, I still kept the router for it's intended purpose as I got it to work, finally.

1. You have to keep checking your configuration after you save, even if you save and reboot. On several occasions and in several different parts of the configuration, I would set a parameter and save, rebooting where necessary, only to find that the change never really got committed to the router. I saw others complain about this and I thought that maybe they just didn't notice they didn't actually hit the "save" button. Well, I can attest that this does happen as it happened to me. Sometimes it would take 3 or 4 attempts to save a parameter before it was finally committed to the router. Weird. Just don't assume you "know for sure I changed it." You have to keep checking to make sure.
2. You can't subnet off of the byte boundary (i.e., subnets other than /8, /16, or /24) without a massive performance hit. WIth nothing else on the wireless at the time, the TV had rasterization problems. For those who are really techie, please note: the 2.4GHz and 5GHz network were moved to empty channels, so no competition for performance from neighbors!
3. For the life of me, I cannot get the DHCP range of IP addresses to be anything other than what the router puts in there by default, no matter how many times I save it and reboot. To me, this is a security problem as will as a network management problem.
4. Buggy. The router worked fine when I configured it in one location. When it was time to move it to another, NOTHING had to change. When I booted the router, TCP connections would not work at all even though ICMP and UDP got through. Nothing in my router's configuration singled out TCP. Reboots did not help. I had to factory reset (full factory reset, not partial) and put in the same exact configuration. After that, TCP worked fine again. Frustrating!
5. I do not see anything about 802.11 AC speeds in the configuration despite this being an AC router (or so I thought). It only went up to 802.11n. Looking back at the Amazon listing, it lists this router as 802.11 A/C. I didn't notice the slash or maybe at the time I thought it was a typo. Now I do not. I have to look up exactly what that means. If I had devices performing at 802.11 AC now or in the future, I would have returned the router. This network is going to be fairly stagnet with the same devices for years to come.
6. I did experience the DNS problems (not resolving) that is well documented in the forums. I knew at the time that there might be a DNS resolving problem and a subnet masking problem. When I experienced the network delays along with the DNS resolver delays, I changed both the DNS configuration and the subnet masking at the same time with the intent to go back to find out which was really at fault for the DNS resolving delays. When I found the performance hit from the subnet masking, it didn't matter if it caused the DNS resolving problem (by introducing network delays on the DNS packets). I just kept the configuration as is. As such, I never went back and reverted my DNS configuration to see if the DNS resolving problem was being caused solely by the DNS configuration. I am done with the stupid problems and at that point, I didn't care just as long as the router was finally doing it's job. If you want to know what I did with the DNS: I put in OpenDNS servers as the resolvers choosing not to use the Telco's DNS resolvers because of bias in return information. When the resolving problem occurred, I simply put the Telco's DNS resolver IP's back in the configuration.

Please note: Do not forget to put in all the available firmware updates. TP-LINK just released the firmware update for the Krack vulnerability. This is a non-starter if you do not put this firmware update in! This is not a ding against the router. Although late, at least TP-Link has patched the worst wireless vulnerability in the world (yes, practically all wireless devices on earth are vulnerable unless you patch.... I'm not exaggerating either! look it up if you don't believe me.)

Other than all that, the router is now performing satisfactorily, but admittedly, the 12 wireless devices being managed are very low traffic shy of 2 streaming devices)

If you intend on using this for dd-wrt or other open source firmware (which will void your warranty), please look up the plausibility of it working. It's well documented that there is a major issue that may cause you to brick your C9 router. As such, I'm keeping this on TP-Link firmware until the warranty period is over. I'll find another router for dd-wrt with less risk.
text_fidelity_b: TP-Link AC1900 Smart Wireless Router - Beamforming Dual Band Gigabit WiFi Internet Routers for Home, High Speed, Long Range, Ideal for Gaming (Archer C9)

text_fidelity_a:
Verso Prologue Case Cover for Kindle Fire, Tan (does not fit Kindle Fire HD) At first glance, this appears to be an elegant folio cover for tablets; it has an authentic-looking antique book design with embossing on the faux leather, some "gold" leafing, and real top-stitching, and it fits nicely on a book shelf (great disguise if you think you need to hide your device for whatever reason). While the design is lovely and the black microfiber supposedly prevents your screen from getting scratched, the way the tablet is held in is by four elastic straps that do an ok job, but I feel in time will wear out. Because of that concern, the design gets 4/5 stars

The function of this folio is to give the tablet a different look and ease of portability without fear of it breaking. It also helps serve as a dust cover for those who have tablets that don't always use them. This is not made for all terrain, though it's good and light weight enough for public transport. Parks and other minor recreational places are ok. I wouldn't take this folio camping or to the beach do to fear of destroying both the folio and tablet. Even though there is a cover there is a minor opening that doesn't really stay closed with the tablet in it. This folio doesn't really appear to protect a tablet from accidental drops. For every day use, this gets a 3.5/5, and for not-so every day use (rougher environments), it's closer to 1/5, so bear that in mind when deciding what case to buy.

The positive thing about this folio is that it fits most 7.1 inch tablets It did fit the Galaxy Tab 7.1 and the original kindle with keyboard. I would recommend an accessories pack to go along with the folio, since screen protector is a must! Over all for a folio I would give it 3.5/5 rounded up to 4. While is is beautiful, it only keeps to the basics of what a tablet user needs.
text_fidelity_b: Verso Prologue Case Cover for Kindle Fire, Tan (does not fit Kindle Fire HD)

Echo Dot (3rd Gen) - Smart speaker with Alexa - Heather Gray This is the the second child of my Echo Show 2nd Gen. and my first Echo 2nd Gen. Speaker. A 2nd Gen Dot, Dottin, is their first child. There is also the Aunt of first 2nd Echo 2nd Gen., an Uncle Fire Stick-who brought his two Fire Stick children, and a distant cousin, the Echo Auto. Needless to say, Alexa runs the house!! This 3rd Gen Dot is so great.... Please don't tell Dottin, but she is in danger of being adopted out or, (gasp) traded in, for another 3rd gen Dot. She had just not been pulling her weight in the family lately.
This little 3rg Gen Dot, or Dottie, wish we could call her that... was the perfect fit for our second bathroom. I mean, who can go to the bathroom and take a shower or do your business, without a little music, listening to a book or playing a game? And, suppose you have a smart thermostat and you can't make a run for it when your in the buff and/or soaking wet? You can just tell Alexa to take care of it. So many needs for a Dot in a bathroom, especially a 3rd Gen!!
The sound is a big upgrade from the 2 gen Dot, and I have had no need for a second speaker to enjoy it during a shower. It is super responsive, and hears you, even from a good distance through the house. I've actually had to name it "Echo", because it sometimes would answer when I would be a room away with the door closed.
The upgrade is really nice and I'm glad I got this little gem. She's a welcomed addition to our happy and continuously growing Alexa family.
text_fidelity_b: Echo Dot (3rd Gen) - Smart speaker with Alexa - Heather Gray

Wacom Bamboo Splash Pen Tablet (CTL471) Just a few days ago I finally decided it was time to give my old Genius 8x6 MousePen up. It was time to upgrade to a Wacom. I browsed for a day or two trying to decide what would best suit me, and after a lot of thought I decided this would be the tablet I purchased. It arrived the earliest day it said it would arrive, and that was a treat.

After I opened it up I thought this tablet would be too small since my other one was a bit bigger, but I tested it out in one of the programs that came with it, ArtRage Studio, and was very surprised. I barely realized the drawing space was small, and it was very comfortable and felt very natural to be drawing on. The tablet itself does not take up much space at all, and it's very light and small enough to be easy to work around. ArtRage Studio is also a very nice bonus. It's a great alternative to Photoshop and other programs (I actually see myself using this program more than my Photoshop). The Splash also came with three spare pen nibs for when your current one wears down.

The pen is also very nice in that it doesn't use batteries, and it also fits comfortably in your hand.

I am a little disappointed that this isn't compatible with a wireless connection, but the cord on the tablet really isn't that obtrusive.

I'm very happy with my very first Wacom product, and I hope I can upgrade once more in a few years.
text_fidelity_b: Wacom Bamboo Splash Pen Tablet (CTL471)

USB Type C Cable, Marge Plus USB C Cable 3 Pack (6Ft) These worked well when they worked. The first cable quit working after two and a half months. When I woke up, my phone showed me a notification saying that unsafe charging is detected and should unplug the charger. I figured this was an anomaly, so I ignored the notification and then replugged my phone that night. Immediately I received the same notification. Not wanting my new phone to be damaged over a cable I purchased on Amazon, I replaced the charging cable with another one from the pack.

Not even 6 weeks later, the same exact thing happened. My phone would immediately halt charging and notify me that what was plugged in was unsafe. That's fine. I had a third! Right? Welp. I used that third cord for a short while. Then it would not work until I twisted and turned the cable in a certain way. If I moved my phone at all, the cable would stop charging. If the cord was not in a specific position I wouldn't be able to charge my phone.

As insane as it sounds, I had to charge my brick charger with this ridiculous cord, while the brick charged my phone (see picture) with the original brick charger cable. I am incredibly disappointed with these chargers. This comes as a mild surprise because the micro USB chargers I purchased lasted *at least 1 year*.

Jabra Evolve 65e Wireless Neckband Headset, Link 370, MS-Optimized – Bluetooth Headset with up to 13 Hours of Battery Life – Superior Sound for Calls and Music – Passive Noise Cancelling Headset I ordered the 'Jabra Evolve 65e UC & Link 370 Wireless Professional Earbuds' as I'm a sucker for trying out new wireless earbuds. I've tried various different types. Some that are "truly wireless", some like these that have the connected wire around the neck. These Jabra Evolve 65e earbuds are really pretty amazing for what they are. Sound is great but not booming with bass. They are crisp yet not loud. There is really no sound isolation as the buds don't fit snug in the ear, (even trying the included different size tips and wings) but that seems to be on purpose. As from I can tell from reading about these, is that they are meant to allow some outside sound, so that if you are say jogging, you should be able to hear to be safe right? Now with that said, I see the purpose and the market for these earbuds, and there is absolute value to these.
Pairing these to my Android mobile phone was an absolute breeze. Also, using the USB Bluetooth adapter on my Chromebook made pairing these super simple as well.
Call quality is on par with most wireless earbuds. It's good, but not the same as just using your phone obviously but better than some "cheap" buds I've tried. These are definitely built with the Jabra quality you would expect and I'm overall impressed.
They fit comfortably and secure and I've had no issue with them popping out, but then again I'm not a jogger. They are easy to fit into your ears, unlike others that I've had that take a bit of twisting to get the fit just right.
The app is nice and works well but as with most apps like this, it's gimmicky. I mean I've played with it a bit at first but any more, I just pop the buds in and go, and haven't used the app in quite a while.
So to summarize, these are great earbuds if you don't need "truly wireless" and you don't need sound isolation.
text_fidelity_b: Jabra Evolve 65e Wireless Neckband Headset, Link 370, MS-Optimized – Bluetooth Headset with up to 13 Hours of Battery Life – Superior Sound for Calls and Music – Passive Noise Cancelling Headset

I find screen touchpad typing difficult and I have pretty big hands. The keys on this are quite nice. Very good positive feel and comparable to most laptop keyboards. Complete set of Android function keys that cover just about everything. No need to be touching the screen. I wish the mouse pad was just a bit better. It's more than functional I guess. It's not bad, but it isn't great either. But I'm not a big fan of mouse pads anyway so I might be a bit over critical in this regard. .

The unit connects and disconnects nicely and has a lock lever which latches automatically. You can open it to about a 140 degree angle which makes getting a comforatble viewing angle possible in virtually any situation. If feels quite solid with no free play. Nice snug fit.

It gives you another battery too that adds 4.5 hours of uptime. You also get a standard sized USB 2.0 port and SD card reader. The USB port can operate in "host mode" allowing you to connect a variety of devices that should couple automatically. Can't say that I've used the USB a lot yet.

It is a very nice addition to a great tablet that gives you a laptop PC feel. It is tapered a little in thickness being a bit thicker at the back, but overall not much thicker than the tablet itself. Folded closed with the TF700 attached it's about 3/4 inch thick at the most and makes a nice sleek package. Connected together the two weigh right at 2.5 lbs.

The current price seems a bit high compared to other tablet's docking ports, but the keyboard is superior and the other features are quite nice. It's a worthwhile addition. I'd give it 5 stars if it were about $50 cheaper.

It’s important to note this is not capable of Quick Charging - each port can only deliver 2A (and test accurately at this level) but I don’t see this as an issue as I use chargers to charge my devices not my hub.

This is an outstanding hub that is made to last many years and perform at blazing speeds and optimum efficiency without fail.

This is an outstanding hub.

text_fidelity_a: Echo Dot (2nd Generation) - Smart speaker with Alexa - White So... I own both the tower and now several dots.  Of course the dots are more reasonably priced, however, the speaker ability is really where it's vastly different.  Obviously the tower is much better in the speaker department.  However, I did find that there is a cordless speaker you can buy to go with your 2nd gen dot that is an improvement and still at lower price point than the tower when combined with the cost of the dot. (Mokcao cordless speaker - amazon sells it too) Because the dots are so reasonably priced we have them in all 3 major rooms and use the cordless speaker to drop one dot in and take it outside to our sunroom when we like.  Over all, I am pleased with both my tower AND dots... but probably will stick to dot purchases in the future because of the price point.  I would say if you've been on the fence, the dot is well worth a try.  It's very easy to set up, you will need to download the app, also easy to follow step by step setups.  Once you're hooked up you will be amazed at how often you use Alexa.  At our house she helps me keep track of where I am supposed to be every day... timers... night time meditation... the occasional argument and even plays games with us as well as much needed comedic relief.  It may not be "necessary" to have Alexa, but I am always surprised at how often we use her assistance.  It's nice and worth it to us.  I never hesitate to update my reviews should new info seem useful.
text_fidelity_b: Echo Dot (2nd Generation) - Smart speaker with Alexa - White

text_fidelity_a:
CTVISION 4K 8MP Home Business Wired Security Camera Systems,8-Channel 4K 8MP PoE Network Video Recorder(4TB HDD),8pc 4K (4X1080P) Outdoor Dome PoE IP Camera,Free App,P2P Cloud,Onvif,Video Surveillance [[VIDEOID:5b880a1d8f11ab783ee7340a330164be]] I ordered the ‘CTVISION 4K 8MP Home Business Wired Security Camera Systems,8-Channel 4K 8MP PoE Network Video Recorder(4TB HDD),8pc 4K (4X1080P) Outdoor Dome PoE IP Camera,Free App,P2P Cloud,Onvif,Video Surveillance’ for review and would like to share my thoughts.

I will lay this out as pros and cons and give some final thoughts.

Pros: The kit as a whole is well made.
Cameras are well made.
The 4tb hard drive is a good name brand and seems to be performing quite well.
The video quality is good.
The kit comes with 8X good quality 50 foot CAT5 cables (more on this in the cons)

Cons: The included cables are only 50 feet each. In a home install, if you are trying to run cameras to all corners of your house, 50 feet is not long enough in my case. I only used three of these cables. I had to buy more cable (CAT6) for the longer runs.
Although the cameras are well made, because they are of the Dome type, if you adjust the cameras to point at much of an angle, you run into issues at night when the IR lights turn on. This causes the IR lights to reflect back at the cameras (See attached video) The best angle for the cameras are to point straight down or at a very slight angle.
Speaking of angles, these cameras only have a 90 degree diagonal viewing angle which was a little disappointing.
When viewing the live feed, sometimes the video feed gets distorted for a couple of seconds.
The software of the NVR is a little overwhelming and hard to navigate. This is probably due to the fact that I have never used this type of system before. There are a lot of options in the Software which does not work with these specific cameras, such as Human Detection or PTZ (Pan Tilt Zoom). Not having the PTZ is really no big deal but it would have been nice to have the Human Detection so that the cameras don’t alarm when the wind blows the trees and shrubs.
There is an option to send an email when there is motion detected on the cameras but I was never able to get that to work.
Although there is an email option, I would have liked to see a text option.

Overall I am actually happy with this kit. It at least provides peace-of-mind knowing that the cameras are always recording and with the included 4tb hard drive in this kit, it provides many hours of footage. I hope that this was somewhat helpful.
text_fidelity_b: CTVISION 4K 8MP Home Business Wired Security Camera Systems,8-Channel 4K 8MP PoE Network Video Recorder(4TB HDD),8pc 4K (4X1080P) Outdoor Dome PoE IP Camera,Free App,P2P Cloud,Onvif,Video Surveillance

Byron Statics Portable CD Boombox with AM/FM Radio, Top Loading CD, 1W RMS x 2 Stereo Speaker, Aux-in Jack, LCD Display, AC110-120V Operated (KBB-250) Likes.

1. Simple to use.
2. My IPhone recognized the radio immediately, establishing a bluetooth connection. It never cut out.
3. The sound quality for both music and voice is very good. OTA radio less so, but that’s understood.

Dislikes.

I wish it was smaller. It’s much larger than I expected. Make sure you have enough room.

Overall.

The radio works flawlessly, both with four C batteries and by plugging it into an outlet. I tested the sound quality by playing some songs that I had downloaded from You Tube Premium, to my iPhone. The sound was very good. I then tested voice quality by playing an Audible book through it. It was Neil Gaiman’s voice, and the sound quality was very good. The volume was fine.

The bluetooth connection.
I set the radio to bluetooth, then went to bluetooth settings on my IPhone. The IPhone immediately recognized the radio, and paired. I played both songs and the Audible books, using this connection. I ordered the radio in order to listen to hours of Audible books at night. I usually fall asleep while listening, and it played throughout the night. That way, I wouldn’t be exhausting my IPhone battery constantly, as it uses a lot less battery life, when it doesn’t need to pump out volume. Minuses

text_fidelity_a:
D-Link Pan & Tilt Wi-Fi Camera (DCS-5009L) (Discontinued by Manufacturer) This camera is yet another product made in China and sold here in the United States for prices equivalent to what we'd pay if the thing was actually made in the USA, which IT IS NOT. The plastic it's made with seems cheap and brittle.

The setup instructions are WRONG and can lead you through a lengthy hell to install and configure the camera. The camera DID NOT HAVE THE MOST CURRENT SOFTWARE and I was forced through an update TWICE because the first one was the wrong one. Yes, the wrong one was recommended on their website. It took a second pass to get the correct version. Speaking of their website, it's a real mess, difficult to navigate, impossible to locate what you need on it, and just plain annoying. Tech support is mostly via email and the one time I did get a human, he didn't know much about anything.

You may want to use the camera's web interface to set up security and so forth. The GOTCHA is the cameras use Java and Java is going to drive your internet security software, firewall and virus protection wild. Java is known to be a welcome mat announcing your computer is open for all manner of malware, virus infections and so on. My security software blocked the install entirely.

Access to the camera remotely is via the D-Link website through an account you set up. To see the camera's video you must go to the website, log in and then view the camera. As video goes from camera to the D-Link website and then to you via your mobile device, the panning and zooming is jerky due to the lag in the up and download of the signal.

If you're looking for a security camera to use while traveling, or out for an evening, this will take care of things--barely. If you want a home security system with multiple cameras, go for a dedicated system with hard-wired cameras, a DVR and a solid wall around it for security. This camera is a toy compared to industrial or home-grade security.
text_fidelity_b: D-Link Pan & Tilt Wi-Fi Camera (DCS-5009L) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

Logitech 910000153 V220 Cordless Optical Mouse for Notebooks [[VIDEOID:c6148faf689d084cd73b4a5362755ed1]] Just playing around with my first ever video review, so please bear with me.

The V220 is a pretty good mouse considering the price tag. It's compact and rugged looking, with rubber pads at the sides for a good grip.

It only needs one AA battery (Note: the diagram is misleading with regard to the way to put in the battery. You should see the + side when you're closing the top)

You can use it for desktops as well as laptops.

There's storage space for the receiver at the bottom, and once you click it into place, the mouse automatically shuts off.

The ridged rubber wheel is the noisy variety, and goes click, click, click, all the way home.

It comes with no software, but gives you a link to the website where you can get a download to make the mouse do tricks. After the download, you can scroll from side to side, click and roll to zoom, and if you give it a shove, it can even roll over and play dead.

It has a warning light to tell you when your battery needs changing.

It doesn't come with a case or pouch, but looks like it can handle going commando just fine.

In summary, it's a good mouse, but not a great mouse - and well worth the price.

Amanda Richards, October 9, 2007
text_fidelity_b: Logitech 910000153 V220 Cordless Optical Mouse for Notebooks

text_fidelity_a:
D-Link Day & Night Wi-Fi Camera with Remote Viewing (DCS-932L) (Discontinued by Manufacturer) First of all, the D-Link camera is relatively easy to set up - always the one to play with techie stuff first, my husband had it up and running in a flash (well almost a flash). Just attach the supplied cable to your computer, run the CD and follow the simple instructions and you're good to go. According to the instructions, you have two options to set up the camera: wirelessly or wired. Naturally, my husband tried the wireless option first, which didn't work because it claimed (spuriously, we believe) that it couldn't find the network, so he had to resort to the other method, which worked right away. We're using a Linksys wireless router.

The camera works quite well indoors where the intensity of the ambient light is generally much lower than outdoors. However, in the brighter outdoor light it is difficult to discern what you're looking at (is it a bird, is it a plane?). The colour is not the best, but then again, it ain't a Nikon 7000. There is some amount of adjustment that can be done online to change the settings, but you'll need to create an online account/register your camera first with D-Link at [...] This is also necessary if you want to view your camera remotely. Strange enough, whenever I try to access the camera online, I get a message telling me that the application needs an earlier version of Java. However, after hitting <Run> for the next three dialogue boxes or so that pop up, it will display the picture. I tried accessing the camera from outside my home network but was unable to do so. Maybe firewall issues?? (Too much effort required to check this). There is also an iPod app that is quite good, minus sound.

Night vision was surprisingly good too. In the dark, the images were shades of grey, but in brighter conditions, the colour returned. Four LED lights lit up whenever the night vision was activated (could be an issue if you wanted to place it somewhere discrete).

On the down side, the camera has to be plugged into an electrical socket to work, and the cord it came with is very short. This means you have to either place it near an electrical outlet or use an extension cord. This would obviously have limitations on where you can place it. It also has to be connected to your home network whether wired or wireless.

While in theory it could be used as a security camera, it has to be powered 24/7, so if you live in a country or area prone to an uneven power supply which could damage sensitive equipment, then you may want to consider that before getting it or you may need to install additional equipment such as line conditioners/UPS to protect your equipment.

The sound is not very good. In fact, after a few hours use it started to make a clicking sound in an endless loop.

Recommended for limited applications such as keeping an eye on kids (or pets, or pesky guests), or when you're avoiding (hiding from) certain people who come calling at your gate, but not as a dedicated security system.

Amanda Richards, June 29, 2011
text_fidelity_b: D-Link Day & Night Wi-Fi Camera with Remote Viewing (DCS-932L) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
WD_BLACK 1TB SN850 NVMe Internal Gaming SSD Solid State Drive with Heatsink - Works with Playstation 5, Gen4 PCIe, M.2 2280, Up to 7,000 MB/s - WDS100T1XHE I originally bought a WD 2tb NVME to use as my main OS, but it would not migrate/clone properly even with their own software. I downloaded a 3rd party migration/cloning software and that didnt work either. I tried nearly everything I could for 1.5 days! I even tried backing up/restoring manually and then repairing. Nothing worked. It was a complete waste of time. I didnt even learn anything in the process other than learning that I should go with a company that has a readily available comprehensive solution that doesn't needlessly waste your valuable time. 1.5 days down the drain.

So I ended up migrating my Samsung 1tb NVME to a new Samsung 2tb NVME and it couldnt have been any easier. < 15 minutes, very quick! I previously, migrated from a corsair SSD to Samsung 1tb NVME (when i couldnt get another SSD to migrate properly), and that was flawless as well. Why didnt I initially go with the Samsung 2tb instead of WD? Press had positive news about it. I am not a fanboy so I like to try different solutions. That was a mistake. What's apparent to me after this experience is that Samsung is better than all their competitors at providing a comprehensive package of the best hardware and software. The experience is FLAWLESS. I havent had any issues with any of their storage solutions to date.

Why did I bother writing this review? Because I wasted 1.5 days. Something has to come out of it. Maybe itll help someone or maybe WD will get their act together and work on their cloning/migration software because the hardware seems to be fantastic.

Disclosure, I bought and paid for everything myself and I still own HDs/SSDs/MicroSds by WD (only old HDs), Sandisk (microsds, ssds), Seagate (HD), Samsung (SSDs, Micro SDs and NVMEs).
text_fidelity_b: WD_BLACK 1TB SN850 NVMe Internal Gaming SSD Solid State Drive with Heatsink - Works with Playstation 5, Gen4 PCIe, M.2 2280, Up to 7,000 MB/s - WDS100T1XHE

text_fidelity_a:
SYSFUN Single Bluetooth Wireless Earbud, Mini Invisible in-Ear Wireless Bluetooth Headphone 12 Hours Super Long Battery Life Suitable for Sports Work and Sleep - Black First thing I notice when I opened this package is that there is no charging case like you get with other true-wireless earbuds. You just get the earbud and a micro-USB charging cable. No charging case means you cannot easily recharge it on the go if the battery runs out; you need to plug it in to a USB charger. There is also no hard case to protect the earbud and keep it clean when not in use.

Two ear tips are included in the package. One is small size and the other is medium/large. They work OK, but are not as secure or comfortable as the memory foam ear tips that come with better quality earbuds.

The earbud paired easily with my Android phone. Sound quality is not good enough for music (to my ears), but fine for voice playback (like podcasts, news/sports, or phone calls). Volume is not really great, but sound quality is not noisy so you can max out your phone volume without hurting your ears.

The Amazon product description says you should get 12 hours of playback time, but the instruction sheet in the package says 5-6 hours of playback time. I listened to voice podcasts at close to maximum volume for 10 hours and still had 50% battery left. If you listen to music, battery life will probably be worse.

This earbud does not have any water resistance rating like you get with most better quality earbuds.

I often use a single earbud when I am running so I can hear car traffic with my other ear. This earbud is good enough for my purposes so far, but it is probably the worst quality wireless earbud that I own. 3.5 stars.
text_fidelity_b: SYSFUN Single Bluetooth Wireless Earbud, Mini Invisible in-Ear Wireless Bluetooth Headphone 12 Hours Super Long Battery Life Suitable for Sports Work and Sleep - Black

text_fidelity_a:
ARCTIC Breeze Pro USB Desktop Fan with 4-Port USB Hub This review covers two different models of the Arctic fan:

>>>>>>>>>>>>>>Model with USB hub:
I have been using the original ARCTIC Breeze for a while and have been very pleased with its performance, and especially pleased with how quiet it runs. The Pro model builds on that and adds a few more useful features.

Unlike the original model which had a bendable stem with a USB plug on the end, the Pro has a base so the fan can be positioned away from the USB port on the PC. The attached power cord is a little over 5 feet long, making it possible to put the fan on my desk and plug it into the PC on the floor.

The base also has 4 USB input ports, so it works as a USB hub. It has a 5V power input jack if you want to turn this into an active hub. The power adapter to do so is NOT included.

Unlike the single-speed original version, this has a knob so you can vary the speed. It's not precise, but there is a somewhat noticeable difference between low and high. It's a continually variable speed - you can turn the dial to whatever speed you like.

Best of all, it's just as quiet, if not quieter, than the original model. That's the biggest plus for me by far, since the cheap USB fans make a racket. This just makes a low-pitched hum. The build quality is solid - the base is sturdy, and the bendable arm holds its position well.

One negative: the packaging. It's in a clam shell package that is a major, major pain to open!

While it's more expensive than the original, the added benefits of being able to position it on a desk and use it as a hub makes the upgrade worth considering. Highly recommend.

>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>USA EDITION:
I've have (and use) a couple other Arctic USB fans and have been 100% satisfied with them. This new version (their "USA Edition") has a couple of improvements over past designs.

The base is a metal plate which increases the fan's stability when you're bending the stem to point the fan. The on/off/speed dial switch no longer has a lit LED ring around it. I never found the lit LED ring to be bothersome on the other Arctic fans, so having or not having it is not a big deal to me.

The base also does away with the USB hub connections that other models have. That's keeps the base more streamlined and allows it to have a lower profile. It also does away with the clam shell packaging, instead using a very easy to open box.

The build quality of this, like the other Arctic fans I have, is excellent. The stem is bendy by stays put where you want it; the operating sound is pretty hushed; the on/off/speed control works well. The overall design is attractive, with a red/white/blue color scheme and graphics.

It moves a surprising amount of air. No, it won't blow your hair back as a Vornado fan will, but this makes a noticeable difference in circulating air. The size makes it very easy to find a spot on your desk to position it.

While I can't speak to the long-term reliability of this as of yet, I expect it will last for some time. I have an Arctic fan similar to this that I've been using almost daily for the past 1+ years, and it still works as good as it did when new.

Looks good, works well, and easy to use. Highly recommend.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: ARCTIC Breeze Pro USB Desktop Fan with 4-Port USB Hub

text_fidelity_a:
Ring Video Doorbell (1st Gen) – 720p HD video, motion activated alerts, easy installation – Satin Nickel The lifetime warranty on this doorbell is the real deal. This is a very well-supported doorbell.

I was having issues with holiday season package thieves and a non-working wireless doorbell. Ring is the only video doorbell I could find that will work wirelessly. The first one had battery issues. Replaced no problem. The second one had sound issues. Replaced no problem. The third on works FLAWLESSLY. I absolutely love it.

The smart motion sensor works well. I see everyone who comes onto my porch, but not my neighbors' porches (three doors lined up on one big house). Two way sound is mostly good -> if it's really windy, it's hard to hear sometimes. The video is way better than I thought it would be. I can see well enough on my phone, but if I download and watch on my computer, it is very impressive.

I signed up for the cloud recording - it's the least expensive pay service of any of my security cameras, and it has been reliable over the few weeks I have been using it. The doorbell is also conspicuous enough to act as a deterrent. I've had a couple of alerts where people looked like they were going to come up the steps and then changed their minds. Both my postal carrier and my UPS driver said that a lot of their stops have these, and they really like them.

Bottom line: It took a couple of tries, but I am one hundred percent happy with this doorbell. If you have an issue, use the warranty. It's a real thing.

text_fidelity_a: JBL On Tour Portable Speaker System ( Black ) This is a great, little device!  First of all, I think it's beautiful and sleek, and easy to use.  Just slide it open, plug in the cable that links to your iPod, and if you are using batteries, that's it, good to go.  Just plug in the AC cord if you aren't using batteries.  Uses 4 AAA batteries, so the batteries are small, don't add any noticeable weight to the unit.  Your iPod stays in it's own protective case, no fitting it onto a dock slot.  I've had one Altec Lansing speaker set and one Sonic Impact speaker set that the slot became damaged, so I'm glad I don't deal with that anymore.  This thing is light, small, about the size of a very, VERY large eyeglasses case so it packs very nicely in a purse, carry-on or suitcase, even better if you can get along without the bulky AC cord and just use batteries.  But it's about the sound, isn't it?  If you are looking for sound in your hotel room, or bathroom, mobile home, bedroom, kitchen, garage, den, etc., you are going to LOVE this little guy, and it will be more than loud enough, it can crank!  The sound is really great!  It looks great, performs great, and I just bought another one for a friend going to Mexico in a week.  Now, if you want a loud, space-filling but still portable speaker, get the In-Motion IM9 unit, as I did also.  I have both.  The IM9 is too big for the suitcase, and it's REALLY heavy, but it's screaming loud, great for the backyard or tailgating or any party setting, and very compact and portable while protecting the iPod within it's great loading system.  But this JBL is your OTHER speaker system for light weight travel or just to fill a room at home.  If you don't love it as I do, I don't know what planet you live on!
text_fidelity_b: JBL On Tour Portable Speaker System ( Black )

text_fidelity_a:
Anker Ergonomic Optical USB Wired Vertical Mouse 1000/1600 DPI, 5 Buttons CE100 It takes some getting used to. I have three of these Anker ergos. Two are wireless and are in use at work. One is wired and on my gaming rig at home.

Gaming: My normal mouse is a Logitech gaming mouse which had been my go to for many years. It was fast accurate and had plenty of built in controls for everything I needed. This mouse also has all of the relevant controls and the resolution button is less likely to get accidentally hit than on the Logitech. It does still get hit here and there though. I also find that the vertical style while more comfortable is not as ideal for gaming but honestly speaking is a small niggle in that the comfort is far more appreciated than the slightly awkward hand position (as movements need to be very fast). Is this up to par with other premium gaming controllers? I have my doubts, but it is certainly comfortable and as a wired controller is adequate for sure.

Everyday: Just yes. Especially considering the value. It is both affordable as an ergonomic mouse and comfortable. You may need to make adjustments to your seating angle as the tendency is for this mouse to be most comfortable when your forearm is almost flat on the desk surface.

Look and feel: It is not an especially heavy mouse. But it does have a level of refinement expected on something more costly. It is also well designed and not obscenely gaudy like a lot of products these days. The rubbery matte surface is pleasant and tactile and the buttons are responsive and easy to actuate. The mouse is somewhat full-sized. I don't want to say large because I have small-medium hands and I can use this just fine, but by no means do I have small hands. Those who have small hands might find this more of a challenge to use though I don't doubt you'll get used to it. The primary buttons and grip would be fine, but the locations of the scroll wheel and the forward nav button are a bit of a reach.

Like I said I have three of these in various formats and love them all. Other than my ultra compact travel mouse, these are used on all of my home and work devices. At such a reasonable cost you can't lose by at least trying it.
text_fidelity_b: Anker Ergonomic Optical USB Wired Vertical Mouse 1000/1600 DPI, 5 Buttons CE100

text_fidelity_a:
D-FantiX Digital Battery Tester, Universal Battery Checker Household Battery Testers for AAA AA C D 9V 1.5V Small Batteries Button Cell (Model: BT-168D) This will tell you if a battery is good or bad. However since it has no internal power source, it uses the power of the battery you are testing to give you a reading. This requires a power drain on the battery you are testing, which will ALWAYS give you inaccurate results. If you take a very small battery, such as a 1.5 V watch battery that is 1/3 depleted, this may be as mush as 30% off on the low side. Example, I checked a 1.5 V watch batty and this showed 1.0 V. Using a high end, self powered volt meter, the battery shoed 1.4V. That is a huge difference.

So again, it will show you a dead battery, but so will dropping a battery on end on a hard surface, If it bounces its dead, if it thuds and does not bounce, its good. Work on all AA, AAA, C, D. batteries.
text_fidelity_b: D-FantiX Digital Battery Tester, Universal Battery Checker Household Battery Testers for AAA AA C D 9V 1.5V Small Batteries Button Cell (Model: BT-168D)

Victrola Retro Wood Bluetooth FM/AM Radio with Rotary Dial, Espresso I got the "acceptable" unit for total $17 (sorry), one foot pad is missing, I'll innovate. Firstly, I had wanted the chrome front but couldn't afford it and didn't want to wait a week; when I saw this used for the price I just pushed the button.

From the pictures you would think the front is all matte black, it is not. It's actually a very dark brown and the controls are a dark bronze, in shiny metal; closer to chrome aesthetic and looks far better with more tones than the photos would suggest. I'm actually happy I bought the darker color now seeing it. I tried to capture this on my pic, but it's too dark and still doesn't capture the wonderful appearance.

Plugging it in and turning it on was instantly satisfying, easy to use controls, no stiffness, good quality, lights work, radio is a deep amber or orange. Nice wood, looks and operates easily and great.

Tuning to a somewhat hard to get classical station locally was surprisingly easy and the signal came in loud and clear, unlike the other radios I've tried from Amazon. It felt like an old stereo where you didn't have to give it thought and was instinctive in the first 30 seconds without the difficulty and poor reception and static and crackling of tuning and volume controls or pops of turning it on nearly all cheap modern radios have now.

Bluetooth connected and performed seamlessly, perhaps a little softer than the radio but not horribly so. And the sound... On both radio and bluetooth the sound quality is superb; *just* enough bass without being muddy and the treble is good and clear. Bass in the voices and high pitches in the music, and very loud without screech or static at still low volume on the knob, with room-filling sound on FM and bluetooth.

This is the most pleasing product I've purchased from Amazon in a long time, especially in the radio category.

Update: After trying several others, I bought a second one! Like New $21. The only thing I notice is neither sits perfectly evenly, there's a slight wobble, even with all four feet pads. No biggie. Love the radio, excellent big sound, bass, but not muddy. Best radio on Amazon, and a true "table radio".

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Fire (Previous Generation - 1st) I love the new Fire I just received. Many delights and surprises including exceptionally fast browser, sharp, clear screen, lovely colors, all the pizazz you get on and iPad for $300 less. So what's not to like? My Kindles are research and study tools, with entertainment a distant 5th or 6th interest so my review is heavily weighted in that direction.

1. I cannot believe Fire has NO SUPPORT for Collections. My Kindle Touch does. Good grief it's only a stack of folders that any operating system beyond MS-DOS can create or delete! Where is Collections support and when, OH when is it coming? Serious limitation to the usefulness as the library grows. Fortunately, I have Calibre on my PC and can routinely add or subtract items to the Fire library and keep the number of current books smaller. But that is a lousy option since I do a good deal of translation work and never know when I might need one of the reference items on the Fire. I bought Fire because of the browsing capability which is so rudimentary in Kindle Touch as to be non-usable, except of course to buy books from Amazon! Well, I have to agree, they are in the business of selling books, music, movies, etc. So that is fine on the Touch. The browser is quite good, much faster than I imagined.

2. Even more stunning a defect is the inability to switch DEFAULT dictionaries, which I can do on my Kindle Touch with a few touches of the screen. I have several foreign language digital dictionaries and depending upon the work I'm doing at the time, set up one or the other. (Even Kindle for PC has a choice of 6 different dictionaries now! I wish they would add Latin but they haven't yet.)

As I study, these Kindles are study tools 90% of the time, both 1.) and 2.) are uncomfortable drawbacks. Sure I can get a foreign word into the browser and search the web, IF I'm near a good wireless hotspot or at home. Takes several steps and is awkward with the virtual keyboard to type anything that is at all complicated. I am told that the Sony comparable ebook tablet can handle Collections, don't know about the dictionary. Should have looked at it.

Edited:Added after about 10 days experience: Sad to say I sent it back.

The lack of default dictionary selection, glare off the screen and eye strain from fighting glare were too much. As a study tool my Kindle Touch is far better and will do most everything I want. I do not watch videos, store photos, listen to music. Those are things the Fire does remarkably well. My Kindle Touch is a work horse and the Fire had functions of no use to me. I knew going in that might be the case. If I ever decide to become a movie buff or listener of music on the go, then I'll get another Fire. By that time I am sure it will be improved too.

I still give it 4 stars for what it does, one star short of perfect because of what I said in my original review.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Fire (Previous Generation - 1st)

text_fidelity_a:
Sony MDR-ED21LP Fontopia In-The-Ear Headphones (Discontinued by Manufacturer) These are really, really high quality earbuds, especially for the price. The sound quality is actually pretty amazing. I had a middling-quality pair of those "Inked" earbuds attached to my laptop at work. The sound quality was always disappointing, but I had sort of assumed that it was probably due to the laptop sound card, etc. Then today I attached my new Sony Fontopias and wow...what a difference! Yes, they have bass boost, but not so much that it overwhelms the music.

These headphones are also surprisingly comfortable. They aren't the typical in-ear shape that gets jammed all the way into your ear, but there's a little more to them than the default "sort of hang in the outer part of your ear" that you get with the default iPod earbuds, for example. I like the hybrid, in-between quality and they fit me pretty well. They're not noise-cancelling, but the sound is so good that I really don't notice other office sounds (not even my disgusting cubicle neighbor who eats cookies like the Cookie Monster and sounds completely disgusting - now you know why I need to listen to music at work!). I'm so happy with the sound quality and comfort of these headphones, I'm willing to give then four stars in spite of one very major drawback:

THE CORD IS RIDICULOUSLY SHORT.

I have NEVER seen such a short cord on any pair of headphones, earbuds, headset, etc. that I have owned. I measured the cord from the jack to the point where the "Y" that goes to each individual bud starts, and it is barely 2 feet. TWO FEET! People, that is SHORT. So I'm going to go to Radio Shack at lunch today and buy an extension cord/adapter. So unless you're going to sit right next to the source you are connecting the headphones to, whether it's a computer or MP3 player or stereo, you'll need to add the cost of an extension cable to the price. Trust me - it's way too short as sold, like it wouldn't even stretch from my iPod in a backpack to my ears if I was walking around.

Otherwise, awesome headphones.
text_fidelity_b: Sony MDR-ED21LP Fontopia In-The-Ear Headphones (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

Not bad, about what I imagined having never used a gel glob like this before (but having wanted to for a long time!).

I have only used it on my keyboard. It is my main reason for acquiring it. I am always grossed out by how my keyboard looks. I sometimes use canned air (but ran out) and disinfectant wipes. I really just wanted to see if I could do better with a cleaning glob. I just wanted to know!

It did a great job with the surface of the keys. They look polished and shiny, and not at all greasy nor grimy. I would say it took more effort to get further down the sides, but I may have been too careful/light with my effort. I think next time I will really pressed into the keys and hopefully I can just work the stuff down the sides easier. Going forward, I would still use canned air to get anything out that is deeper down below the keys. And, still using a disinfectant wipe is a good idea these days. I think I will use this as maintenance rather than for going after a super gross keyboard. I like the scent- it smells fresh and clean. Doesn't linger, but while using it it is rather nice.

The look of it after using it to clean my keyboard really makes me want to hurl. I am not sure how often this can be reused, or if it would be better as a one time project use. I mean, it is meant to be used over and over, just not sure if I want to. Again, I think I like the idea of using it as a maintenance item if I plan to use it over and over. There is a little diagram on the container showing how to check if it needs replacing. It doesn't say much, but I surmise that if it goes from the bright color to a dark color, then it needs to be replaced.

Anyway, I think it is worth the try. It really does grab onto the nasty things and pulls it off/out. This wasn't too pricey, and I think stuff like this could be added on to a themed gift- like a car/truck lovers gift, an office supplies gift, and so on. Who knows.

There is some info on the container (a small clear plastic container with screw on lid, and labeling all around) that I will list here:

Directions say:
-- "Do not rub just press!" as well as, "Use with body hands" (lost in translation? maybe means both hands, or put your body into it?)

--Absorbs dirt and dust in cavities. Ideal for all devices and surfaces

--Keep away from direct sunlight and keep in a dry place. Keep away from children, don't eat it

--Ingredients:
Vegetable gum, Bactericide, Quaternium, fragrance, glycerin.

--Made in China
text_fidelity_b: Cleaning Gel 160G, Dust Cleaning Mud for Car, Car Accessories, Keyboard Printers Cameras PC Tablet Laptop Airpods Case Cleaner

text_fidelity_a:
Osprey Nova Women's Laptop Backpack I walk to school everyday, it's about a 30minute walk. That combined with all the time walking to different buildings once I'm at school, is a lot of time to get cozy with this backpack.

A little back story, I previously owned a unisex North face backpack, I got rid of it because it was too big and hurt my back. I downsized to a women's North face. It was better but it still didn't seem very comfortable and never felt very light even with few items in it.

Cut to this backpack, it's a women's backpack so it's made smaller. (Also I'm 5'7" 120lbs so I'm not terribly small bit still). This backpack feels lighter than others, I think it has to do with the frame, it's very comfortable on. I typically have 2 binders and two medium sized textbooks in my backpack, occasionally I'll bring my laptop. With everything in it, It doesn't irritate my lower back or shoulders after hours of wear.

The backpack also comes with 2 straps on the side that allows you to compress it in even further. When your stuff is closer to your back, and not hanging far out, it's a lot more comfortable. There are several pockets, a large padded pocket for your laptop, another for your books and such and 2 smaller but still very spacious pockets, as well as an interior pocket and nonzippered outer pocket.

The pockets do zip all the way around, but the straps will need to be unbuckled to do this. I'm not gonna lie, I'm very lazy and have not unbuckled the straps since getting this item, (it's been a month), and I've been able to get my books/laptop in and out without a problem.

The pockets for waterbottles are nice and deep so your water bottle won't fall out, and there's also a strap on either side to secure it even further.

The chest strap on this is awesome too. It doesn't compress your chest in an awkward or uncomfortable way which is something I always look for.

The shoulder straps and back are vented so it's been really great for me, a very sweaty person walking in the summer time. Haha

Overall I think this backpack is awesome! I've already recommended it to my school friends, looks like Osprey is my new go to backpack brand!:D
text_fidelity_b: Osprey Nova Women's Laptop Backpack

text_fidelity_a:
Kensington Pro Fit® Ergo Vertical Wireless Trackball (K75326WW), Black, 3" x 4" x 6.1" Initially, I liked the ergonomic design. It put much less pressure on my wrist than the Logitech trackball I've been using for many years. Unfortunately, when I started up World of Warcraft, I noticed the Kensington trackball button mapping software disabled the ability to use more than one button at once. I found the same detriment in Overwatch where multiple buttons often need to be pressed simultaneously. When I contacted the company, they sent me an email. The following is a direct quote from their email:
"Thank you for contacting Kensington Technical Support.

We would like to inform you that these trackballs are designed for basic office use and will not work on gaming applications.

We appreciate your time and patience."

To me, this came across as rather rude. This, coupled with the fact that this very mouse shows up in searches for gaming trackball mouse made me extremely disappointed and, in fact, somewhat angry. I feel Kensington needs to do any or all of the following. 1. Fix the software to make their hardware gaming inclusive. 2. Stop advertising their non-gaming devices as gaming devices (I feel this is blatant false advertising.) 3. Ask customers how they could fix issues rather than giving them a short, curt email to inform us that we, apparently, are idiots for expecting their devices to work as advertised.

Bottom line: I do not recommend buying this product unless all you intend to use it for is emails and youtube.
text_fidelity_b: Kensington Pro Fit® Ergo Vertical Wireless Trackball (K75326WW), Black, 3" x 4" x 6.1"

I have this one in a Windows 7 machine, and it's use is transparent and I don't do all those tweaks you read about and I read all about them.

If you want to keep it simple unplug all drives but the DVD, if installing that way, and the SSD drive. Install windows 7. Profit. Than do two things. Make sure disk level indexing is off (which you should be doing anyway) this is under your C: drive properties right under where it says Compress this drive to save space. The indexing shouldn't be set if you installed the way I said, but check anyway. This will not effect windows indexing (which I vote for leaving on even on a SSD drive)

Then update your drives firmware.

Don't worry about cache and indexing, super fetch and all that. Just let Win 7 set all that all up. and all that.

Don't worry about hibernate. Use hibernate if you want, or don't, but you don't need to change it since you are running on a SSD. Same with system restore if you have the room, and you like having it on, leave it on. This drive will automatically over-provision 7% of the drive so you don't need to set that.

Windows will set up your drive just fine. If you want to go research it all and make your own decisions, that's fine I did the same thing. And the above 'simple' installation was what I decided on. (I did 3 separate installations working through various options).. I have tweaks I do, but they are tweaks I do SSD or no SSD.

A lot of information about SSD drives is based on small drives and older controllers. You don't need to worry about how long your drive will last. It will last longer than you will have your computer. Look up the tests on this on the internet to understand how little of an issue this really is. A lot of what is written about SSD's is written by enthusiasts/gamers who are into tweaking systems. If, like me, you like doing this kind of research, great. Otherwise just install windows and use your drive SDD drive like any other drive.
text_fidelity_b: Samsung Electronics 840 EVO-Series 120GB 2.5-Inch SATA III Single Unit Version Internal Solid State Drive MZ-7TE120BW

text_fidelity_a:
Uniden BCD536HP HomePatrol Series Digital Phase 2 Base/Mobile Scanner with HPDB and Wi-Fi & (BC23A) Bearcat 15-Watt Amplified External Communications Speaker This review is for the Uniden BCD436HP I see reviews here for other radios, so not to be confused.
I used Amazon Prime Now to get the radio to me, in less than 1 hour (about 45 minutes) the delivery person was knocking on my door with my new receiver, wow, I was highly impressed and I will always check to see if Prime Now is available for all my deliveries from now on.....
So, the radio....
This receiver has a 4 gig SD card preloaded with every known frequency with text for the entire US and Canada. They have software called Sentinel you install on your PC and this is your gateway to all updates and firmware and it can control your radios SD card any way you like. Sentinel has an extensive database of all frequencies and let me say this again, all frequencies have text description included which is the most highly advanced scanner database system I have ever seen and I have owned scanner receivers most of my adult life, (long time)..
This is a digital receiver using the latest technology available. It can monitor any analog or digital TX (with some exceptions, like encrypted signals) and gives you extensive control over what you're listening to. There are FCC laws regarding what is legal and not legal to monitor and Uniden has got us right up to the maximum legally allowed to be monitored by civilians. If you are law enforcement persons you will have much more powerful receivers available to you capable of Cell phone conversation monitoring etc., things no civilian should even be interested in.
There is another version of this Uniden radio, the BCD536 which is a tabletop version. If you have large powerful outdoor weatherproof antennas the BCD536 is a good option and it is completely transferable to vehicle dash mount and back from your work desk to your vehicle.
I like this handheld BCD436 best personally for my purposes.
This is basically a plug and play receiver. It comes with 3 2300 milliamp rechargeable batteries, load those, charge them or just leave radio plugged in, enter your zip and you're in. Well theoretically that's how it works, in the real world? No.
When you first receive the radio I would suggest positioning yourself in front of your PC. Have the paper manual, the radio, you and your PC right there in front of you. Get ready to read and learn your radios keyboard layout and what these great, well thought out keys can do for you. You will learn, trust me, you will quickly come to love this radio.
Some cons:
No wall charger adopter included. You can charge from your PC's USB ports but you will need a wall charger with USB port. Most of us have several of these around the house from old cell phones etc. They work fine.
This unit should come with a nice wall charger adopter. That's really the only con, not to bad really.
Antennas:
Your ability to scan and receive signals on any scanner is proportionate to your antennas. The more robust and correct (correct meaning size, materials used etc).. You will need some nice antennas for this nice radio to increase your scanning powers. Amazon has some nice antennas, scannermaster.com has some also. Your local radio shop retailer will have some also. The included rubber ducky antenna is garbage, toss it from across the room to your garbage can, see if you can make a rim shot. Like I said, I have been playing with scanners for many years so I have many antennas to pick from.
Verdict:
This is without a doubt, the most powerful handheld scanning receiver available from any manufacturer. It is the luxury sedan of the scanning receiver world. It is easy and robust. It is backed up by Uniden's Sentinel software which will future proof your radio for many years to come.
I give Uniden 5 stars for this winner.
I give Amazon 5 stars for Prime Now 1 hour shipping, also a winner.

Edit:
Okay some people are wondering what the best accessories are for this receiver.
Go to scannermaster.com and look for the Austin Condor All-Band Portable BNC Antenna and the SpectrumForce Desk Mount for One Portable Scanner.
The Condor all band antenna is unsurpassed.
The desktop stand holds your handheld at the perfect viewing angle, you can listen and see all text clearly right beside your computer.
See my photos. The photos ended up sideways.... trying to fix this..... Amazon, can you turn my photos upright?
text_fidelity_b: Uniden BCD536HP HomePatrol Series Digital Phase 2 Base/Mobile Scanner with HPDB and Wi-Fi & (BC23A) Bearcat 15-Watt Amplified External Communications Speaker

I’ve tried using different plug ins for the treadmill and computer, not it (my husband is an electrician and assured me this was not it.). When testing this theory and intentionally removing power and plugging back in, the monitor had a setting box pup-up…. Because it lost powder, great. But when the screen flashes that box doesn’t come up which tells me it’s not loosing power-it’s loosing a connection to the computer. After messing with it and becoming frustrated, I thought I heard a little zap noise where it’s located so when I started feeling around I got a very minor static shock on my finger. So my Inspector Gadget hat told me that I was generating static electricity with my treadmill and for some reason it was collecting on this dual monitor plug and basically shorting itself out. (This only happens when walking on the treadmill.) So, in all my Mom-knowing madness, I wrapped it up in a dryer sheet and it actually works for the most part. It might flash a couple times in a day but my office smells amazing. I will be looking for something else for sure. It’s really annoying.

text_fidelity_a:
ClearClick HD Video Capture Box Ultimate (4K Edition) - Record and Stream Video from HDMI (Up to 4K30) and AV Video Sources - No Computer Required THE GOOD:
--------------
* It will do as it says.. capture videos from your sources.
* Video quality seems fine to me. I'm not that picky, the stuff I record isn't important.
* You can install a micro SD card, or connect a hard drive via usb.

THE BAD:
-----------
* Consistent with their products, they cut corners when it comes to the remote control. It's just a terrible clunky experience. I can't even put into words what's wrong with it. I guess there is a delay. So if you're impatient, you'll be pressing too many buttons, and you'll be in the wrong menu, navigate to the wrong places, enable the wrong features, etc. So my advice is to be patient. Press the button you want to press, then wait a week for it to respond. I don't know what inner components make a great remote control. Whatever they are, they are not inside ClearClick remotes. I've reviewed some of their other Clearclick products that are $150 and less, and so I was more forgiving. But at $250, really? You're going to still skimp out on the remote at this price range?

* If you toggle into PLAYBACK mode... good luck getting out of it. Back button doesn't work, and it's always thinking you want to delete files. Everytime I escape playback mode, I'm relieved, but also have no clue how I got out.

* Power on/off is weird. There are scenarios that will make your heart stop because you'll think the device shorted out. Just like their terrible remotes, I've noticed this power issue with their other models too. The quirk is this... sometimes when you power off and on too quickly, it just goes dead. It will not respond for a long time. Don't panic. Stop pushing the power button. Just unplug everything. The hard drive, the HDMI, the power, unplug everything. Go walk your dog, and when you come back, and connect everything again, it will power up. This happens to other Clearclick devices I have, so when it happened with this device, I didn't panic. I knew what was up.

* Power port is micro usb. Again, at $250, I'd like to see USB-C. Micro usb is antiquated, and their cords are prone to get damaged.

* You will need a HDMI splitter to bypass HDCP, as well as be able to turn off your Clearclick when you're not recording, and still watch TV. In my scenario... my source goes into my splitter, and my splitter has TWO outs. One goes into the Clearclick, and the other goes to my projector. This way, I can turn off my Clearclick if I'm not recording, and still watch my projector. If I connect the source directly to the Clearclick, and then go OUT from the Clearclick to my projector, then I would get their ugly icons on my projector. In my pictures, the source is my Nvidia Shield, you'll notice a row of white icons at the top. There is no option to hide these icons in passthrough mode. So if you use the Clearclick as a passthrough, you will get those ugly icons on your big screen. So even if you're recording sources that do not need a HDMI splitter. I'd still get one anyway because using the hdmi passthrough is not pretty. However, the good thing is that the files you record, will not have those icons.

In conclusion, if this weren't a Vine item, I would send it back. Having said all that, it's possible that my expectations may be unreasonable for a very niche product. If a big company like Sony or Samsung create a polished standalone capture device like this, maybe it'd be $500-$600. In which case, you'd be pretty happy with the ClearClick. If you learn to live with the quirks, it's a nifty piece of tech. Hopefully, they can improve on the user experience through firmware updates. I'll go 3-Stars this time.
text_fidelity_b: ClearClick HD Video Capture Box Ultimate (4K Edition) - Record and Stream Video from HDMI (Up to 4K30) and AV Video Sources - No Computer Required

ZZN Bluetooth Running Headphones, Wireless Waterproof IPX7 Earbuds with Earhooks,Sport Earbuds in Ear,16H Playtime Sweatproof Headphones for Gym Running Workout, Comfortable Ear Hook PROS

1. Excellent sound for both treble and bass,
2. Well made, of durable construction.
3. Attractive appearance.
4. Water/sweat resistant.
5. Lithium, rechargeable battery, with a charge that lasts up to 16 hours.
6. Excellent range.
7. Built-in microphone, so you can use it to dictate with a voice recognition app or make phone calls. The sound quality for calls is excellent.
8. Comes with an attractive carrying case which is black with red trim .

CONS

2. The fit around the ears is a bit too tight for my own personal comfort. However, this is probably an inevitability, given the fact that earhooks have to fit firmly in order to not fall off during vigorous exercise.
3. There is no information offered on the country of origin of the manufacturer or, in fact, any information offered at all.

NEUTRAL

1. Be aware that, as is the case for all rechargeable, lithium batteries, the battery in this product will ultimately need to be discarded with hazardous waste.

Osprey Apogee Men's Laptop Backpack , Kraken Blue This is a nice backpack. It’s lightweight and the color is very cool. It’s like a blue grey with dark teal straps. It’s not flashy but it’s not boring black either.
The 2 bottle holders on the side are very sleek and well done. It’s always annoying when bottles fall out is the side because they are too small - that won’t happen with these.
There are 3 pockets. The stash pocket is the only pocket that can be accessed if the compression hooks are used. The compression hooks can be tucked away when they aren’t needed which is nice - I don’t like having a bunch of hooks out catching on things.
The stash pocket isn’t huge but it’s a good size - can fit hand in easily and then it’s about 11” across.
The 2nd area is deep but isn’t wide. It will hold a jacket or sweater and then has 3 slotted pockets for a phone/ passport/ notebook. Outer 2 pockets are 3.5” and middle pocket is 4” wide. All pockets are about 5.5” deep.
The middle compartment also has a red clip. It’s easy to use and I like to use these to attach my keys so they don’t drop to the bottom of bags.
The main compartment is pretty big.
It has a double sided padded laptop area that measures 10.5” wide.
On top of the laptop is a tablet area that is single sided padded that measures 10” wide and up to 13” tall. The tablet area isn’t as deep as the laptop area. This area would also work for documents.
The top handle is well padded and sewn. Below that there is a two sided opening for headphone cords or even a plug to charge your laptop/tablet.
The main straps are well padded and adjustable. They have a top strap and a lower strap for comfort and security.
The zippers are all well quality and have a material flap over the top so it should keep anything inside pretty dry.
text_fidelity_b: Osprey Apogee Men's Laptop Backpack , Kraken Blue

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Fire (Previous Generation - 1st) The kindle fire is a nice e reader and has a lot of bonuses such as the beautiful color displays. Still, I'm not sure it was quite what I was expecting. I'm not thrilled with the battery life as I usually can't finish a book before the battery is dead. It does not have a camera which I kind of think is lame since most devices even less expensive ones do. I'm disappointed that there is not free 3g connect like there is with the dx. Also, the Kindle Fire tends to get really heavy after you have held it for a while. It seems they could have found a way to make it as attractive and still lighter. The screen tends to have a bit of a glare when you are outdoors and sometimes it is hard to read through.

Since you have to have wifi to watch the movies and they are only free with a prime membership. This means you are responsible for paying for the internet gigs needed to use these features, which is okay if you have an unlimited internet package, but a lot of people don't.

Over all I think the fire is a good test model but there could be a lot of upgrades to make it a more practical device and get the utmost enjoyment out of it.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Fire (Previous Generation - 1st)

To me, these are advantages over the Logitech K350 I've been using, which has a curved, not split, key layout and a spongy feel when typing.

What I don't like, and what was pretty much a dealbreaker to me (I thought about returning it almost immediately) is the "wrist rest." It is short and rolls off steeply and provides no wrist support at all, unless you like typing with your wrist positioned lower than your knuckles and your hands bent upwards from the wrist. The recommended position is wrist level with the knuckles, which is called the "neutral" position. I personally prefer typing with my wrists positioned slightly higher than my knuckles.

Look at the product photos and notice that the typist doesn't even have his wrist on the wrist rest. He or she is using a hover hand technique, I guess to make things look more ergonomic or something, because if their wrists were actually on the wrist rest, their hands would be obviously bent upwards at the wrists to reach the keys.

I'm at a loss as to why many keyboard manufacturers (including Logitech with the K350) provide legs to raise the back of the keyboard and don't provide anything to raise the front. That just makes the "backwards" bend at the wrist even more pronounced.

This Periboard keyboard is no exception to that. It has foldaway legs at the back and none in the front. But even if it had legs to raise the front, it wouldn't provide much improvement. I raised the front a couple of inches with a foam wedge I use for keyboard support, and the wrist rest was still so low I pressed the spacebar when reaching for the F2 key.

I even tried adding foam wrist rests but the built-in rest is so steep and short it actually interferes with using a really functional rest. I even tried using wearable wrist rests---which are kind of annoying on their own since they aren't all that stable---and the steep slope and short length of the built-in wrist rest made that a less than effective solution. This keyboard might have been a lot better if it had no built-in wrist rest at all. That way you could use your own and set it up just like you like it.

It's disappointing, actually. I like the key action and layout, but the wrist rest pretty much nerfs the whole thing. I may keep it and experiment with solutions from time to time. I might even see if I can cut off the built-in rest and replace it with something made of wood or something, or just get it out of the way so I can use some other effective wrist rest.

In the meantime, I'm probably going to stick with the spongy-action, non-split Logitech K350. In fact I'm typing this review on it, though I would have liked to use the Periboard 512. But until I come up with a better wrist rest solution it's just easier to use the K350.

And a couple more quick points, comparing this keyboard to the K350, this keyboard is wired while the K350 is wireless. The overall footprint of both (length and width) is almost the same. I personally don't use or need the multimedia keys on either.

Because of the better key action and, to me, better key layout, if it had a better wrist rest, or none at all, this Periboard 512 might have become my go-to keyboard.
text_fidelity_b: Perixx Periboard-512 Ergonomic Split Keyboard - Natural Ergonomic Design - Black - Bulky Size 19.09"x9.29"x1.73", US English Layout

text_fidelity_a:
Echo Dot (2nd Generation) - Smart speaker with Alexa - White Great price and fun to play with. If you're interested in smart home technology this is a great place to start since it's easy to use and connect to other devices down the road. I bought several as Christmas gifts and when people figured out how to use it they loved it. The built in speaker is ok, I knew it wasn't as good as the more expensive Echo so I wasn't disappointed. If you already have a Bluetooth speaker or sound quality isn't a huge factor for you out of the box then you can't beat the price. I don't have any issues hearing Alexa's responses with the built in speaker, but when I want to listen to music I just connect my Bluetooth speaker (very easy to do) and can move it around the house with no problems. We have a dot on each floor of our house (2 stories) that are located in the most used areas. I keep a Bluetooth speaker in our bedroom and use the Alexa remote to interact with the Dot in our tv room since she can't hear me as well. This allows you to still connect to, and hear Alexa, without having to yell and strain to hear her.

The shopping list and to do list feature I really like since I'm horrible at writing down what we need around the house before I go shopping. I just tell her what to add to my list as I notice it, and it instantly shows up in the Alexa app which I can open when I get to the store and add/delete items. I also love these features to capture random things I want to research later like book titles, tv shows, serial numbers for parts etc that I might forget if I don't have it written down somewhere.

The only reason I didn't give the dot 5 stars is because most of the skills that are available right now leave a lot to be desired. I'm sure down the road this will improve but there isn't a lot to choose from right now that has a lot of practical use. Like a lot of people I would prefer Alexa be able to answer questions based on a Google search rather than having to enable skills for different things. If I want to know what flu symptons are she doesn't understand what I'm asking. But when you factor in everything she can do, and what she can connect with, then the dot is definitely still worth purchasing based on the price.
text_fidelity_b: Echo Dot (2nd Generation) - Smart speaker with Alexa - White
